findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed two sanitizer buckets measure 0ppm quaternary ammonia during today’s visit. The PIC was informed and the bucket was replaced, measuring 200ppm quaternary ammonia with a test strip. Inspector recommends increasing the frequency of bucket replacement. Printed labels are used to indicate the discard time for sanitizer, but the bucket measuring 0ppm was not due to expire for another two hours.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the green shelves holding pizza dough and rolling cart holding raw chicken to be soiled with microbial growth. The PIC was informed and plans to deep clean/sanitize the shelving. Ensure staff are monitoring cleanliness in the cooler and sanitizing surfaces frequently to prevent the accumulation of microbial growth. Ensure the shelves are clean to sight and touch prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the bottom shelf of the stainless steel table across from the chicken fryers to be rusted and in disrepair. This shelf is used to store extra broaster equipment, which comes in direct contact with food. Ensure this table is sealed or replaced prior to the next routine inspection.

Inspector also observed the green wire shelves in the dish area to be rusted and in disrepair. These shelves hold clean dishes, which are direct food contact surfaces. Ensure these shelves are sealed or replaced prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the dish machine measure a maximum temperature of 150.8F after multiple repeated attempts. The PIC discovered that the booster was not functioning properly. The PIC contacted support and fixed the machine. The machine then measured 161F with the dish puck. Ensure staff are monitoring the machine to prevent future violations.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.112(A) Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Hot Water Sanitization Temperatures. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, in a mechanical operation, the temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 90°C (194°F), or less than: (1) For a stationary rack, single temperature machine, 74°C (165°F); or (2) For all other machines, 82°C (180°F).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
The inspector observed the following time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods to be held past their 7-day date mark:
1. Cauliflower (discard date 1/8/26)
2. Alfredo sauce (discard date 1/6/26)
3. Ranch dressing (discard date 16/2026)

The PIC was informed and these items were voluntarily discarded. Ensure staff are checking date marks at the beginning and end of each day to prevent the use of expired items.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee don a new pair of gloves without handwashing. Education was conducted regarding proper hand washing. Ensure staff are hand washing before donning a new pair of gloves.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed triple sink to measure 0ppm quaternary ammonia. The PIC immediately recognized that the Quat-San bucket under the triple sink was not properly connected; the tubing was not far enough into the sanitizer bucket. The triple sink was drained and refilled, with a quaternary ammonia concentration of 200ppm. The violation is considered corrected on site.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
findings.comment: Observed dish machine in use following violation #16 from the inspection conducted on 3/6/25 being unresolved. The dish machine was out of temperature and inadequate for sanitization. It seems there is a lack of communication between the Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) and the rest of the staff regarding necessary repairs and change of procedure. Ensure the dish staff is informed at all times regarding proper dish handling and sanitization as well as any changes to procedure. A spot check will be conducted on 3/17/2025 along with the follow-up on the dish machine to ensure proper communication between CFPM’s and staff.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(L) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (L) EMPLOYEES are properly SANITIZING cleaned multiuse EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS before they are reused, through routine monitoring of solution temperature and exposure time for hot water SANITIZING, and chemical concentration, pH, temperature, and exposure time for chemical SANITIZING.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed dish machine in use following violation #16 from the inspection conducted on 3/6/25 being unresolved. The dish machine was out of temperature and inadequate for sanitization. The PIC confirmed that the dish machine has not been serviced since the previous inspection, and there was no sanitizer in the triple sink. Since the dish machine is still not reaching the minimum temperature for sanitization (165F), it cannot be used to sanitize dishes or equipment. A triple sink with sanitizer was prepared during the inspection. Ensure staff are using the triple sink until the repairs are complete. The original follow-up date for the dish machine, 3/17/2025, still applies.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed 8 containers of cut vegetables in the salad bar cooler and 4 containers of cut vegetables on the salad bar itself to have date marking indicating the food items were past their acceptable serving date. PIC was informed that the containers were out of date, and all 12 containers were voluntarily discarded. findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
findings.comment: Observed floor drain in dish room to be overflowing. Dish machine is routed to floor drain, and drain overflows upon use of machine. PIC stated that this issue is ongoing and has been using a drain snake “when the room floods.” A follow-up is scheduled for 3/10/2025 to ensure drain is operating properly.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Observed CFPM on duty to not have allergen awareness training certification. Provide allergen awareness training certification for all CFPM.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

Milk in the upright cooler as you enter into the kitchen from the drive through area is observed without a date marking. PIC was consulted and stated that the container was opened this past Sunday (11/7/21). Education took place and a date tag was made during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. 

An employee was observed to wash their hands, use a paper towel to turn off the faucet and the use the same paper towel to dry their hands. Employee was then observed to handle food contact surfaces. Hand washing was reviewed with the PIC and they were instructed to ensure that all employees had adequate training to properly wash their hands.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above. 

The cayenne currently used for marinara sauce in the facility is only holding foods at 86F. The equipment is supposed to have water in it (per the PIC) and does not leading to the lower holding temperatures. The sauce was discarded during the inspection and water added to the equipment to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) The blade of the can opener is not clean to sight and touch. Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely (every 4 hours in continuous use or after each use when not in continuous use). Reference 4-601.11(A). Can opener was properly cleaned.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1)  (P) Mashed potato is 120°F. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 135°F, or above. Reviewed hot holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(1).

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text: 3-501.15  (Pf) The method of cooling chicken is inadequate. Observed chicken to be cooling on the counter at 83F with no date or time tag and no active cooling process being utilized. Use one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: placing the food in shallow pans; separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; using containers that facilitate heat transfer; adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Discussed HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.15. Properly time and date tag the cooling chicken. Chicken was discarded.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on the following non food contact surfaces: 1) bottom of pizza crust upright cooler 2) front of hot box at drive up window 3) fronts of pizza prep table and reach in freezer at slotted vent covers 4) bottom of dessert cooler 5) under cabinets at drink station 6) under cabinets at both hot bars 7) top of ice cream machine 8) inside of both hot boxes one holding items for the bar and one being used as storage in the back by ice machine. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent gross soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: 6-501.12 (A & B) (C) Floors are soiled in the facility especially around legs and wheels of the equipment. Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  Reference 6-501.12 (A & B).
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11  (C) Cabinets under the drink station are in gross disrepair. Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.  Reference 6-501.11. Repair replace the cabinets.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment: Observed employee to stabilize pizza with bare hand while cutting. Wash hands a properly glove if needed to cut pizza. Employee was coached at time of inspection. 3-301.11 (P) Food employee used bare hands to handle ready to eat foods. Food employees shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas/tongs, dispensing equipment or single use gloves when handling ready to eat foods. Reference 3-301.11.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Observed can opener to be soiled. 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Observed the blade of the can opener to be soiled with dirt, food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.comment: Observed vinegar and oil at the salad bar to be missing labels. Properly label foods. 3-602.11  (C) Customer self-dispensing foods are not properly labeled. Use a card or sign to label with: 1) manufacturer's label, 2) common name of food, 3) ingredients, and 4) nutrition labeling. Reference 3-602.11.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment: Observed two wet wiping cloths to be sitting on surfaces, not in sanitizer, between uses. Store wiping cloths properly at all times. 3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animal foods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment: Observed a coat to be hanging on a rack holding clean dishes. Store personal items properly so that they can not contaminate lean utensils. 4-904.11  (C) Clean utensils are not protected from contamination at the clean utensil rack in the dish room . Clean utensils and single-service articles shall be handled, displayed and dispensed so that food- and lip-contact surfaces are protected form contamination. Reference 4-904.11.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on the following items: 1. cutting boards at pizza prep, 2. doors to walk in cooler, 3. ice machine lid edge, 4. ice cream machine top, 5. hood vents over fryers 6. fan cover and housing in walk in cooler. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.
